ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: In the quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel CD$, $\angle BCD = 90^\circ$, $AB = AD = 10 \text{cm}$, $BC = 8 \text{cm}$. Point $P$ starts from point $A$ and moves at a constant speed of $3\text{cm/s}$ along the polyline $ABCD$ direction; point $Q$ starts from point $D$ and moves at a constant speed of $2\text{cm/s}$ along the segment $DC$ direction. It is known that both points start simultaneously, and when one point reaches the end, the other point also stops moving, let the motion time be $t (s)$. When the quadrilateral $PBQD$ is a parallelogram, what is the perimeter of the quadrilateral $PBQD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Draw lines $PD$ and $BP$, \\
when the quadrilateral $PBQD$ forms a parallelogram, we have $PB = DQ$, \\
given that point P starts from point A and moves in the direction of the polyline $ABCD$ at a constant speed of $3\text{cm/s}$; point Q starts from point D and moves along the line segment $DC$ at a constant speed of $2\text{cm/s}$, \\
let the time of movement for point P be t seconds, then $AP = 3t$, $DQ = 2t$, \\
$\therefore PB = 10 - 3t$, \\
$\therefore 10 - 3t = 2t$, solving this equation, we find $t = 2$, \\
$\therefore PB = DQ = 10 - 3 \times 2 = 4$, hence $CQ = 16 - 4 = 12$, \\
in $\triangle BCQ$, $BQ = \sqrt{BC^2 + CQ^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 12^2} = 4\sqrt{13}$, \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of the parallelogram $PBQD$ is: $2(PB + BQ) = 2 \times (4 + 4\sqrt{13}) = 8 + 8\sqrt{13}\text{cm}$, \\
$\therefore$ the perimeter of the quadrilateral $PBQD$ is $\boxed{8 + 8\sqrt{13}\text{cm}}$.

Thus the perimeter is $\boxed{8 + 8\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}}$.

raw_record.original_question: In quadrilateral $ABCD$, $AB \parallel CD$, $\angle BCD = 90^\circ$, $AB = AD = 10\text{ cm}$, and $BC = 8\text{ cm}$. Point $P$ starts from $A$ and moves at a constant speed of $3\text{ cm/s}$ along polyline $ABCD$; point $Q$ starts from $D$ and moves at a constant speed of $2\text{ cm/s}$ along segment $DC$. Both points start simultaneously, and when one point reaches the end, the other also stops. Let the motion time be $t$ seconds. When quadrilateral $PBQD$ is a parallelogram, what is the perimeter of quadrilateral $PBQD$?
raw_record.answer: Draw lines $PD$ and $BP$. When quadrilateral $PBQD$ forms a parallelogram, we have $PB = DQ$. Given that point $P$ starts from point $A$ and moves along polyline $ABCD$ at a constant speed of $3\text{ cm/s}$, and point $Q$ starts from point $D$ and moves along segment $DC$ at a constant speed of $2\text{ cm/s}$, let the motion time be $t$ seconds. Then $AP = 3t$, $DQ = 2t$, so $PB = 10 - 3t$. Hence $10 - 3t = 2t$, giving $t = 2$. Therefore $PB = DQ = 10 - 3 \times 2 = 4$, and $CQ = 16 - 4 = 12$. In $\triangle BCQ$, $BQ = \sqrt{BC^2 + CQ^2} = \sqrt{8^2 + 12^2} = 4\sqrt{13}$. Therefore, the perimeter of parallelogram $PBQD$ is $2(PB + BQ) = 2(4 + 4\sqrt{13}) = 8 + 8\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}$. Thus the perimeter is $\boxed{8 + 8\sqrt{13}\text{ cm}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: The figure shows trapezoid-like quadrilateral ABCD with AB as the upper horizontal side and CD as the lower horizontal side, so AB ∥ CD. BC is vertical and perpendicular to CD. AD is slanted. Point P lies on AB and moves to the right from A toward B, while point Q lies on DC and moves to the right from D toward C.

Reasoning: Since BC is perpendicular to CD and AB ∥ CD, the height between the two parallel bases is BC = 8 cm. Also AD = 10 cm, so the horizontal offset from D to A is sqrt(10^2 - 8^2) = sqrt(36) = 6 cm. Because AB = 10 cm, the full lower base is CD = 6 + 10 = 16 cm.

For quadrilateral PBQD to be a parallelogram in the shown order, PB must be parallel to DQ. Since DQ lies on CD, this means P must still be on AB. At time t, point P has traveled AP = 3t, so PB = 10 - 3t. Point Q has traveled DQ = 2t. Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal, so PB = DQ. Thus 10 - 3t = 2t, giving 5t = 10 and t = 2.

Then PB = DQ = 4 cm. Since CD = 16 cm, CQ = 16 - 4 = 12 cm. Triangle BCQ is right with legs BC = 8 cm and CQ = 12 cm, so BQ = sqrt(8^2 + 12^2) = sqrt(208) = 4sqrt(13) cm. Therefore the perimeter of parallelogram PBQD is 2(PB + BQ) = 2(4 + 4sqrt(13)) = 8 + 8sqrt(13) cm.
